scope: Creator-mm execve/execveat replacement, actual group CPU retirement and rekey, failed-image recovery, detached old-mm custody, source pure custody-policy decisions and original process-wide cgroup termination.

concurrency.construction: Original Rc owner prepares and commits at creator-mm custody. Unrelated address spaces continue on existing workers. Original group/inbox and cgroup objects preserve process identity through exec.

remaining_boundaries: Scoped original-owner image construction and communication remain
Dynamic proc path refresh, including openat /proc/self/exe, still returns the cohort
Tracing, policy actions with lifecycle effects and actual namespace/administration/native controls remain explicit
Single-CPU/solo execution retains the coordinated caller path

benchmark.scope: 32 sequential exec/execveat replacements or failed attempts with a concurrent busy sibling. Thread mode reexecutes from nonleader threads after the first replacement. Two untimed warmups per binary/mode/CPU count, seven counterbalanced pairs. Metrics run separately. All builds and local Linux tests ended and the local Linux test instance was stopped before timing. This is a process lifecycle benchmark, not general CPU or Firefox performance. Native macOS controls use the same conditional source compiled for Darwin; Mach-O/system libc and Linux static ELF differ, so OS controls are not an identical-image comparison.
benchmark.native_arm_linux_location: Same ELF copied to local filesystem inside the six-vCPU ARM Linux test instance, not executed from the host shared mount. Seven warm samples per mode; collected separately after builds ended.

lifecycle_regression.scope: 128 two-thread groups: fork/clone, leader exit, final-thread exit and parent wait, alternating ordinary files and private epoll controls. Two untimed warmups per binary/CPU count, then seven counterbalanced pairs per CPU count. Includes structural fork/mm work; not a general CPU or Firefox benchmark. Vfork uses the same prior fixture. Local Linux test instance was stopped and no build ran during timings.

measurement_notes: Two untimed warmups and seven counterbalanced before/after pairs per CPU/mode. Metrics are separate from timing. Builds and the Linux test instance ended before Mac timing.
Native ARM Linux reference executes the same ELF from its local filesystem, not the host shared mount. The earlier shared-mount reference is retained only as a diagnostic.

Darwin controls compile the same conditional source as Mach-O with system libc. Linux uses a static ELF and the CI instance has six vCPUs; these are OS controls, not identical-image or general CPU scores.

Absolute host conditions varied between the short lifecycle and longer vfork samples. The 128-round confirmation is used for vfork acceptance; the short sample is retained without hiding its variance.

The lifecycle_regression.native_arm_linux entry is a reused historical fixture reference, retained for provenance and not used for current absolute comparisons. Acceptance uses the co-measured before/after pairs.

negative_controls.whole_cohort_exec: Disabling exec custody makes the new image fail to run before the epoch returns; the six-case matrix fails at mode 0.
negative_controls.discarded_old_memory: Dropping detached memory loses a late original-backing write; the matrix fails at retained-borrow mode 5.

observed_failure.observation: One full-suite run failed during concurrent builds. A later complete 320-case suite passed, followed by ten standalone passes. Root cause was not established; no timeout or assertion was weakened.

candidate_metadata_note: The measured isolated candidate was compiled before committing and embeds the previous 27b3eba runtime label. Its source files match the committed runtime_revision exactly. The final Dev package is rebuilt with the committed pin; identical-code regression/performance results are reused and the tagged package receives focused smoke checks.
